Assume AC and Countable Choice and adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned temperature $T>0$ kelvins, with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. A finite independent mode list means an integer $m\ge1$ and, for each $r\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, a declared type B or F and an excitation energy $\varepsilon_r>0$ joules. For type B take the one-mode Fock Hilbert space with complete number basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N_0}$ and self-adjoint occupation operator $N_re_n=ne_n$ on its exact diagonal domain as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]]. For type F take $\mathcal H_r=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $f_0,f_1$ and $N_rf_n=nf_n$. In either case put $H_r=\varepsilon_rN_r$, and write $u_{r,n}=e_n$ or $f_n$ according to the factor type. Define $\mathcal H^{(1)}=\mathcal H_1$ and recursively $\mathcal H^{(r+1)}=\mathcal H^{(r)}\widehat\otimes\mathcal H_{r+1}$ by the completed Hilbert tensor construction of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]; let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^{(m)}$. The canonical orthonormal product basis is $u_{\mathbf n}=\bigotimes_r u_{r,n_r}$, indexed by $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_m)\in\mathcal C:=\prod_r\mathcal C_r$, where $\mathcal C_r=\mathbb N_0$ for type B and $\mathcal C_r=\{0,1\}$ for type F. If all factors are F then $\mathcal C$ is finite; otherwise it is countably infinite and is enumerated by increasing $\sum_r n_r$ and lexicographic order within each finite level, which is finite because every $n_r\le\sum_r n_r$. For each factor put $\hat\varepsilon_r=\varepsilon_r/(1\,\mathrm J)$. Define the numerical energy map $\hat E:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R$ by $\hat E(\mathbf n)=\sum_{r=1}^m\hat\varepsilon_rn_r$ and the physical energy $E(\mathbf n)=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat E(\mathbf n)$. Define the numerical self-adjoint diagonal operator $\hat H$ by $\hat Hu_{\mathbf n}=\hat E(\mathbf n)u_{\mathbf n}$ on the exact domain
$$D(\hat H)=\Bigl\{\psi\in\mathcal H:\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathcal C}\hat E(\mathbf n)^2|\langle\psi,u_{\mathbf n}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\};$$
when $\mathcal C$ is finite, $\hat H$ is a finite real diagonal endomorphism and is self-adjoint; when $\mathcal C$ is countably infinite, the diagonal-operator lemma [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] gives $\hat H$ self-adjoint for the displayed enumeration. The physical total energy operator is $H=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H$, with $Hu_{\mathbf n}=E(\mathbf n)u_{\mathbf n}$ and $D(H)=D(\hat H)$; multiplication by a nonzero real scalar preserves self-adjointness.
This sum-energy Hamiltonian with no interaction term is the definition of independence for this quantum model.

For one bosonic mode with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and let $N$ be its dimensionless occupation number. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection as defined above, write $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ and $Z=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta$. Then $0<Z<\infty$ and the joint occupation-basis law is $P_\beta(\mathbf n):=e^{-\beta E(\mathbf n)}/Z$. For each factor $r$, define its marginal law by $P_{\beta,r}(k):=\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathcal C:\,n_r=k}P_\beta(\mathbf n)$. The trace satisfies $Z=\prod_{r=1}^m Z_r$, the joint law factorizes as $P_\beta(\mathbf n)=\prod_{r=1}^m(q_r^{n_r}/Z_r)$, and each marginal mean is the corresponding one-mode mean displayed above. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.

boundaries.reason: Statement requires a nonempty finite mode list m>=1 with positive excitation energies and nonzero factor Hilbert spaces; no empty-list or zero-sector trace formula is asserted.

The finite canonical, maximum-entropy, independent-factorization and finite-bath claims concern the exact finite state spaces and shell-weight assumptions stated in their items. Countable and measurable derivative identities require their local summable or integrable moment envelopes; a lower energy bound alone does not normalize the partition function. The lattice bulk-pressure and concentration claims apply only to the bounded finite-range lattice model and, for concentration, a differentiability point of the limiting log-partition density. The page-level continuum-pressure prerequisite is a distinct interaction model; no stable-tempered continuum limit is inferred from the lattice theorem.

Regular-shell preparation requires a nonempty compact regular level, the normalized coarea measure, and AC; it does not require a globally defined flow. The separate invariant-shell theorem adds a smooth invertible Hamiltonian flow on the full band, with time in seconds, and proves measure invariance only. Neither result implies ergodicity or equality of long-time averages with the shell law. The quantum Gibbs and finite-mode trace identities explicitly assume AC and Countable Choice, a semibounded self-adjoint generator, a positive finite Gibbs trace and the stated moment envelope. In the general quantum branch, the mean, variance and von Neumann entropy are defined by the supplied Gibbs eigenfamily sums, so no unbounded operator-trace product is being asserted. Discrete dephasing is a trace-norm Cesaro limit with degenerate eigenspaces retained, not pointwise relaxation or a Gibbs limit.

Boltzmann microstate entropy, finite Gibbs entropy, von Neumann entropy and the macroscopic entropy function are distinct objects until a model supplies an explicit identification. The statistical value $-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ is not silently identified with a macroscopic Helmholtz or grand potential. Canonical and microcanonical sampling are adopted preparation assumptions. None of the finite probability identities, continuum or lattice pressure limits, shell-invariance results or quantum trace calculations reports an experiment or establishes that nature follows the model.

Assume AC and Countable Choice as required by [[pthm-td-finite-mode-occupation-and-trace-formulas]] and the trace-class suppliers. Take modes indexed by $j\in\mathbb N$, each with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, and let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the set of finite-support occupation sequences $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ with $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. Enumerate $\mathcal F$ by increasing $R(n)=\sum_{j:n_j>0}(j+n_j)$ and lexicographic order of the finite list of nonzero pairs $(j,n_j)$ within each level. Each level is finite because $j,n_j\le R(n)$ on its support, and every configuration occurs; skipping empty levels gives a bijection $\mathbb N\to\mathcal F$. Define
$$\ell^2(\mathcal F):=\Bigl\{c:\mathcal F\to\mathbb C:\sum_{n\in\mathcal F}|c(n)|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad \langle c,d\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F}c(n)\overline{d(n)}.$$
The vector $|n\rangle$ is the indicator of $\{n\}$; these canonical occupation vectors form an orthonormal basis. Relabeling by the displayed enumeration is an isometry with $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb C)$, which is a Hilbert space with its standard basis by [[ex-standard-basis-of-ell-two]]; the definition of square-summable families and their inner product is [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]. Define the bounded positive diagonal Gibbs weight $K_\beta|n\rangle=q^{\sum_jn_j}|n\rangle$. On the subspace with $n_j=0$ for every $j>M$, the corresponding finite-mode partition sum is the trace of that restriction.

Assume AC and Countable Choice for the canonical mode preparation. Let $\mathcal H_1=\mathcal H_2=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, and define the factor number maps by $N_r|0\rangle=0$, $N_r|1\rangle=|1\rangle$. The composite Hilbert space is the finite Hilbert tensor product $\mathcal H_1\widehat\otimes\mathcal H_2\cong\mathbb C^4$ from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with orthonormal product basis $|n_1n_2\rangle$, $n_r\in\{0,1\}$. On this basis define the site-number operators $\mathcal N_1|n_1n_2\rangle=n_1|n_1n_2\rangle$ and $\mathcal N_2|n_1n_2\rangle=n_2|n_1n_2\rangle$. For $T>0$ kelvins set $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log2$ joules and define the noninteracting total Hamiltonian
$$H=\varepsilon(\mathcal N_1+\mathcal N_2),\qquad H|n_1n_2\rangle=\varepsilon(n_1+n_2)|n_1n_2\rangle.$$
The quantum Gibbs preparation at $T$ is used for the thermal comparison, and the closed-system unitary evolution is generated by $H$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$, where $t$ is in seconds and $\hbar>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Start the dynamics in $\rho_0=|00\rangle\langle00|$.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.
